:• '''866Mbps''' - 2-stream 802.11ac device (433Mbps per stream), :• '''300Mbps''' - 2-stream 2.4GHz channel = '''''1200 Mbps'' class'''
{{TagLine|AC1200 Wireless Dual Band USB Adapter}} :{{ProductPage|http://www.tp-link.com/us/products/details/cat-5520_Archer-T4U.html}}{{SupportPage|vendor=TP-LINK|model=Archer-T4U_V1}} "2052500409" and the ''TP-LINK'' logo is silkscreened on the board in the FCC photos. The USB ID for this device is per the driver set for the [[Amped Wireless ACA1]]. :The device description matches up with ''TP-LINK'''s tag line for this device. *[https://makerforce.io/tp-link-archer-t4u-teardown/ ''TP-LINK Archer T4U Teardown'' on '''MakerForce'''] (internal images) :WIP Linux Driver: [https://github.com/ulli-kroll/rtl8821au rtl8821au] • [https://github.com/gnab/rtl8812au rtl8821au] • [https://github.com/diederikdehaas/rtl8812AU rtl8812au] • [https://github.com/Grawp/rtl8812au_rtl8821au rtl8812au_rtl8821au] ===Review of Linux Compatibility=== [http://m.linux-hardware-guide.com/2014-11-02-tp-link-archer-t4u-ac1200-usb-adapter-wifi-802-11bgnac-1200mbits-wpsusb-3-0 TP-Link Archer T4U] is a USB WiFi adapter for WiFi connections to 802.11ac standard. :The stick supports USB 3.0 and has the USB ID: 2357:0101 BUS 002 Device 023: ID 2357:0101 The stick bases on the Realtek RTL8812AU chipset, which currently :is not automatically recognized by the Linux kernel. ====Edimax Driver==== *A driver for the Realtek chipset of the T4U is provided by Edimax. :However, the USB ID of the TP-Link Archer T4U is not known to this driver. :Therefore, a patched version of the Edimax driver exists, where the USB ID was added. ====Open Source Driver==== There is also an open source driver under development. This driver can be downloaded from GitHub: 
git clone https://github.com/abperiasamy/rtl8812AU_8821AU_linux.git
cd rtl8812AU_8821AU_linux/
As of Oct 16, 2016 this driver contains the USB ID of the Archer T4U. The driver can be compiled and installed with: 
make
sudo make install
If the TP-Link Archer T4U is plugged in, the kernel module rtl8812au should be loaded automatically:
